orchestkit · regression fix

The gate I added blocked every future release

#3217 widened the CI build-drift gate to cover README.md and docs/site/lib/generated/. Both are derived from CHANGELOG.md, which release-please writes and never rebuilds. So the gate now fails on the release bot's own output, on every release, forever. #3212 is the first casualty.

The loop

release-please writes CHANGELOG.md
        │
        ├─ README what's-new block      derived, not regenerated
        └─ changelog-data.ts            derived, not regenerated
        │
        ▼
  Build: "Build drift detected!"   the bot cannot run npm run build

Why not just narrow the gate back

Because the widening was doing real work: it caught v9.3.0's stale generated files, and then caught a second stale docs-search-index.ts on the very next PR. Reverting trades one silent-staleness class back for a green board. The right fix is to make the bot's output complete, not to stop looking.

The fix extends a step that already existed

release-please.yml already refreshed README on the release PR.
It just never regenerated the docs-site half.

  + cp scripts/generate-changelog-data.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/..."
  + CHANGELOG_DATA_ROOT="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" node "$RUNNER_TEMP/generate-changelog-data.js"
  - git add README.md
  + DERIVED=(README.md docs/site/lib/generated/changelog-data.ts)
  + git add -- "${DERIVED[@]}"

The CHANGELOG_DATA_ROOT env var mirrors the existing WHATS_NEW_ROOT, and exists for the same security reason: that step deliberately copies generators OUT of the workspace before checking out the release branch, so it never runs code from an unprotected branch with the App token in scope. A trusted copy needs to be told where the workspace is.

Proven, not assumed

SimulationResult
generator copied out, run WITH CHANGELOG_DATA_ROOT wrote 12,119 lines into the workspace
same copy, WITHOUT the env var could not read CHANGELOG, wrote nothing

The second row is the point: it confirms the override is load-bearing rather than decorative, which is the only way to know the trusted-copy path actually works.

Dashboard archetype per playground-visual-standard.md section 0. Regression introduced by #3217, surfaced on #3212, both authored in the same session.
